runs.scope: First full pipeline run — treating all history through v0.2.0 as the scanned range (no prior Git tags exist)
runs.notes: Repo's tracked docs are all <=13 days old (post-v0.2.0 release on 2026-03-31), so no staleness remediation was needed. Untracked files (skills/ and docs/tech-writing-adaptation-plan.md) were excluded from freshness scan because the scanner reads git log timestamps — they will be picked up on the next run after commit. Only 4 commits exist in git history, none using conventional-commit format, so changelog categorization was done by reading the v0.2.0 release body.

runs.scope: Second run after committing the tech-writing skill suite under tag v0.2.0. Scan window: since v0.2.0 tag.
runs.notes: Added an [Unreleased] section to CHANGELOG.md covering commit c41aa41 (tech-writing skill suite). No release notes drafted (no new version cut). Both possibly_stale flags (agent_execution_flow.md, llm_tool_call_compatibility.md) are false positives: the scanner treated the new commit as a 'related code change' because it touched repo-root-adjacent paths, but the commit only added files under skills/ and docs/ — nothing that invalidates those two design docs. This is a finding worth feeding back into the freshness scanner's heuristic (Phase 2 improvement: filter 'related changes' by path overlap with the doc's referenced modules rather than any commit touching the repo).
